questions.skill: Prove and apply theorems about triangles
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Prove that the angles of any triangle ABC add to 180°. Start by drawing the line through B parallel to AC.
questions.prompt_markup: Prove that the angles of any triangle ABC add to 180°. Start by drawing the line through B parallel to AC.
questions.required_method: The parallel line through B makes two angles with BA and BC; each equals ∠A or ∠C because they are alternate interior angles; the three angles at B form a straight angle (180°).
questions.grading_note: Form required: the proof with reasons (parallel postulate, alternate interior angles, straight angle).

questions.skill: Prove and apply theorems about triangles
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Explain why an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.
questions.correct_answer: The exterior angle and the adjacent interior angle form a linear pair, so they add to 180°. The three interior angles also add to 180°. Subtracting the adjacent angle from both shows the exterior angle equals the other two interior angles together.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation that uses the linear pair and the triangle angle sum.

questions.skill: Prove and apply theorems about triangles
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, AB = AC. Prove that ∠B ≅ ∠C. (Draw the bisector of ∠A, meeting BC at D.)
questions.prompt_markup: In triangle ABC, AB = AC. Prove that ∠B ≅ ∠C. (Draw the bisector of ∠A, meeting BC at D.)
questions.required_method: Triangles ABD and ACD are congruent by SAS (AB = AC, ∠BAD = ∠CAD, AD = AD), so the corresponding angles ∠B and ∠C are congruent.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the congruence with its reasons and the corresponding-parts conclusion.
